evals.name: korean-naturalness-deep
evals.expected_output: Korean podcast script that sounds like two real Korean people talking — even with a minimal prompt and no style specification, the default output should have natural spoken Korean with proper fillers, reactions, sentence-ending variety, and conversational rhythm

assertions.name: no-formal-endings
assertions.description: Avoids stiff formal endings that sound like a news anchor
assertions.check: Script does NOT overuse ~합니다, ~입니다, ~습니다 formal endings. Should predominantly use ~거든요, ~잖아요, ~인 거죠, ~인데요, ~이에요, ~네요 etc.

assertions.name: natural-fillers
assertions.description: Contains Korean conversational fillers and reactions
assertions.check: Contains fillers like 음..., 아~, 맞아요, 오~, 진짜요?, 흥미롭네요, 그렇죠, 와, 대박 — distributed naturally, not clustered

assertions.name: sentence-ending-variety
assertions.description: Uses varied sentence endings, not repetitive
assertions.check: Sentence endings vary — mixes ~거든요, ~잖아요, ~인 거예요, ~인데요, ~이에요, ~하더라고요, ~이래요 etc. rather than repeating the same ending

assertions.name: natural-transitions
assertions.description: Topic transitions sound natural, not mechanical
assertions.check: Transitions use natural Korean phrases like '근데 여기서...', '그건 그렇고...', '아 그리고...' rather than stiff connectors

assertions.name: no-translation-artifacts
assertions.description: Doesn't read like translated English
assertions.check: No awkward literal translations from English. Uses Korean-native expressions and word order. For example, uses topic markers (은/는) and object markers naturally, doesn't overuse passive constructions

assertions.name: utterance-length-natural
assertions.description: Each person's turn is a natural conversational length
assertions.check: Most utterances are 1-3 sentences. No long monologues. Person1 (host) has shorter turns with questions/reactions, Person2 (expert) has slightly longer but still conversational turns
